messages:
Tess: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can leadership clarify our short elevator pitch for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Also, how should we frame Redwood's differentiation vs large cloud AI vendors when customers ask?
Mira: Great Q, Tess. Short version: Hosted = fastest time-to-value; Dedicated = predictable throughput & SLAs; Private = compliance/data-control. When in doubt, ask: are they bandwidth-limited, sensitive-data, or SLA-driven? That decides the path.
Arjun: Also add: for models where latency economics matter, Dedicated often gives best TCO because of reserved GPU pools + optimized runtime. Hosted is the gateway — smaller integration effort.
Sam: From sales: emphasize guaranteed latency+SLA for Dedicated with concrete numbers. Customers get nervous about "noisy neighbors" and unpredictable costs. Give them a simple 2-line ROI example.
Kelsey: Could we have a 1-slide cheat sheet for sales: 3 rows (Time-to-value, Predictability, Compliance) with checkmarks per offering? Would make conversations way easier.
Mira: Yes — we should produce that. Public-facing line: "Redwood gives you consistent inference performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can pick the right tradeoff for cost, latency, and control." Keep it short.
Ben: On competitors: don't lead with "we're better than X". Instead, call out concrete differences: unified runtime across environments, cost-aware controls (batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations), and rollouts + observability built-in.
Tess: How do we handle questions like "why not just use cloud provider managed endpoints?"
Arjun: Simple reply: cloud providers excel at generic managed infra, but they rarely offer an inference runtime tuned for LLM economics (smart batching, KV caching, model variants). We invest heavily in kernel/runtime optimizations that materially lower per-token cost.
Sam: Add: support and product experience. We move fast on model onboarding, and our SDKs + console reduce time-to-production. Customers care about predictable billing and a clear path for scale.
Kelsey: For sales collateral: include two small case studies — one PLG startup that went Hosted -> Dedicated for throughput, one regulated customer that needed Private. Concrete numbers sell.
Mira: Agree. Action items: (1) Product to ship 1-slide offering cheat sheet (Arjun/Kelsey), (2) Sales to draft two 1-paragraph case studies (Sam), (3) Marketing to produce the short public-facing line and a 1-pager. I'll review by EOW.
Tess: Thanks — one last ask: can leadership share a sentence on our long-term moat vs cloud vendors?
Mira: Short moat line: "We optimize the entire inference stack — from kernels to routing and observability — so teams get predictable performance and lower unit costs without building ops themselves."
Ben: And for technical audiences, mention our compilation/kernel selection + KV cache and routing layers — they're the real lever for cost at scale.
Sam: 👍 This is helpful for sales playbooks. I'll take the case studies.
Arjun: I'll sync with Runtime to get a concise bullet list of optimizations we can include in the 1-pager.
Tess: Perfect, thanks everyone. deploy-bot: scheduled reminder set for 2026-05-01 to check progress on action items. :bell:
